use_case_name: Define Reference Points and Geometric Areas

claims.content: The trigger is that a C2 JU or a JU capable of generating and maintaining track numbers reports an AOP based on organic data, exchange of LOBs, analysis of EW fix data, or a combination; the unit assumes R² for an emergency point after receiving a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message or after no periodic update for three consecutive update intervals; or a JU with R² initiates a force-tell alert on a reference point, line, or area by setting FT IND in the J3.0 Reference Point message.
The C2 JU has reported the defined point, line, or area using the appropriate J-series message (J3.0 Reference Point, J3.1 Emergency Point, or J3.5 Land (Ground) Point/Track).
The C2 JU is the latest IU to report on the reference or land (ground) point, line, or area, and therefore has R² for it.
The C2 JU, as originator, retains R² for the point, line, or area as long as it remains active and reports the point, line, or area.
If a force-tell alert was initiated by setting FT IND in the J3.0 Reference Point message, all receiving JUs have accepted the alert in their databases.

The C2 JU wants to define a multisided area by reporting it in J3.0 messages on a Network PG, setting the Point/Line/Area Descriptor to value 3 (Multi-point Area), using the Line/Area Continuation Indicator for subsequent points, closing the figure by returning to the initial point, and retaining the initiating Reference TN for subsequent reports.

scope_contract.goal_statement: The C2 JU wants to define a multisided area by reporting it in J3.0 messages on a Network PG, setting the Point/Line/Area Descriptor to value 3 (Multi-point Area), using the Line/Area Continuation Indicator for subsequent points, closing the figure by returning to the initial point, and retaining the initiating Reference TN for subsequent reports.

claims.content: If the C2 JU attempts to define a line or an irregular multisided area (i.e., any shape other than a square, rectangle, circle, or ellipse) by slaving, the slaving operation is forbidden.

If the C2 JU attempts to change the Point Type and/or Point Amplification value of a reference point while retaining the same Reference TN, the change is illegal; however, a Point Amplification value of 'No Statement' may be changed to a non-'No Statement' value while retaining the same Reference TN.
If the EW AOP is formed from a single fix, the same TN shall be retained; if it is formed from two or more fixes, a new TN shall be assigned.
If the C2 JU attempts to assume reporting responsibility for another unit's J3.7 EW Fix, AOP, or LOB report, the assumption is illegal.
If the defined/reported object is a missile impact point and predicted impact has occurred, the C2 JU is not required to continue transmitting it.

missing_aspects: main_flow step divergence points for each exception branch (main_flow was not provided)

claims.content: Diverges from the main-flow step in which the reporting JU reports a geometric area using geodetic latitude/longitude positions: when a square or rectangle (Square/Circle Switch = 1) or a circle or ellipse (Square/Circle Switch = 2) is slaved, the position established by Delta Latitude, 1/Delta Longitude, 1 is the center of that area.

Diverges from the main-flow step in which the C2 JU reports a static point, line, or area: as an alternative to static reporting, moving points, lines, and areas are defined by setting Course and Speed in the J3.0C2 word to values other than No Statement, causing the host to extrapolate the position to the time of transfer.

As an alternative to defining a reference point or geometric area by absolute position, certain reference points and areas may be defined as 'slaved' in a constant position relative to a Related TN by setting the Slaved Indicator to value 1; this establishes a constant true or relative bearing and range from the Related TN.

Diverges from the main-flow step in which the C2 JU selects the appropriate J-series message based on the object type: when the J3.1 Emergency Point message is selected and the Exercise Indicator is set to value 1, the report is for exercise purposes and is not an actual emergency.

Under the rule that changing Point Type/Point Amplification while retaining the same Reference TN is illegal for the C2 JU, a Point Amplification value of 'No Statement' may nevertheless be changed to a non-'No Statement' value and retain the same Reference TN.
Diverges from the main-flow step in which the C2 JU reports a geometric area as a MEZ: when the MEZ is an exercise MEZ, it is reported for exercise purposes only.
The C2 JU determines that the object to be defined is a multisided area and selects the J3.0 Reference Point message to report it.
The C2 JU assigns one or more Track Numbers (TNs) to the area and reports its positions using geodetic latitude/longitude values.
In the initial word of the first J3.0 message, the C2 JU sets the Point/Line/Area Descriptor field to value 3 (Multi-point Area).

The C2 JU sets the Line/Area Continuation Indicator to value 0 in the first J3.0 message and to value 1 (Line/Area Continuation) in the second and all subsequent J3.0 messages, permitting the multisided area to have more than 3 points.
The C2 JU closes the area by transmitting the last point location as the same as the initial point location.

The C2 JU uses the Reference TN of the first J3.0 message (the one with Line/Area Continuation Indicator set to 0) as the only legal identifier for all subsequent references to the area, and transmits the initiating TNs with every report of the area.
The C2 JU transmits the completed J3.0 message(s) in the Surveillance Network PGs.
The C2 JU must have achieved Active status, or have returned to Active status from Inactive status or TDS Failure.
The C2 JU must be capable of generating, maintaining, and assigning one or more Track Numbers (TNs) to each point, line, area, or AOP it reports on the interface.

quality_flags.detail: [mainflow_trigger_continuity] The Trigger is a disjunction of three different starts (AOP reporting, emergency-point R² assumption, force-tell alert initiation), but Main Flow step 1 starts by determining a multisided area and selecting the J3.0 Reference Point message. It never continues the AOP, emergency-point, or force-tell paths, and it never sets FT IND. This is a restart rather than a vertical continuation. The same over-broad Trigger also makes the force-tell postcondition unreachable and implies an R² precondition that Preconditions do not state. (atomic grounding: candidate remains incomplete (The cited cards do not support a discrete 'C2 JU determining' triggering event; they state the goal and the transmission/encoding requirements.; The specific 'J3.0 Reference Point messages' designation is not supported by the cited cards; the supported message context is J3 Surveillance messages / surveillance information in Network PGs.))

[altflow_diverge_points] The alternative-flow branches are not anchored to the supplied main_flow. Several branches state divergence points that do not exist in the main_flow's seven J3.0 multisided-area steps: index 0 references slaving a geometric area to a related TN, indices 2 and 3 reference J3.1 Emergency Point reporting/preparation, index 4 references modifying a reference point, and index 5 references reporting an area as a MEZ. No branch gives a numeric main_flow step anchor, so the divergence points are out of range or unverifiable. (still no supporting evidence after retrieval)

[trigger_preconditions_coverage] The Trigger's force-tell branch requires 'a JU with R²', but Preconditions only assert Active status and TN-generation capability. The C2 JU must already hold R² for the point/line/area before it can initiate a force-tell alert; this required state is absent from Preconditions. (atomic grounding: candidate remains incomplete (The specific actor 'C2 JU' is not supported by the cited evidence; EC-TR-005 supports a generic JU with R², and EC-PO-003 defines R² by the latest reporting IU.))

[mainflow_trigger_continuity] The Trigger lists three different starting situations: AOP reporting, emergency-point R² assumption (J7.0/no-update), and force-tell initiation. Main Flow step 1 starts with a J3.0 multisided-area definition and never continues from the emergency-point or force-tell branches. This is a real restart/gap, and the missing branches also leave corresponding Postconditions (J3.1/J3.5 reporting and force-tell acceptance) unreachable. (atomic grounding: candidate remains incomplete (The trigger alternative about reporting a multisided area in J3.0 messages with Point/Line/Area Descriptor value 3 and Line/Area Continuation Indicator is not supported as a trigger by the cited cards; EC-MF-011 and EC-MF-007 support encoding details in the main flow, not the trigger event.))

[mainflow_trigger_continuity] The trigger claim lists three distinct starting conditions: reporting an AOP, assuming R² for an emergency point after J7.0/no-update, and initiating a force-tell alert by setting FT IND. The main flow, however, is a single J3.0 multisided-area definition sequence. It does not continue the emergency-point branch and never sets FT IND for the force-tell branch, so Main Flow step 1 is a different scenario from those triggers.

[trigger_preconditions_coverage] The force-tell trigger condition requires that the initiating unit already has R² ('a JU with R² initiates a force-tell alert'). Neither precondition claim states that the C2 JU must have R² for the reference point, line, or area before initiating such an alert.

[altflow_diverge_points] Alternative flow claim 5 does not reference any existing main-flow step as a divergence point. It states a point-amplification modification rule without attaching it to one of the seven main-flow steps, so the branch cannot be validated against main_flow.

inconsistency_hints: The goal claim is over-broad relative to the provided main_flow. It promises definition/reporting of points, lines, areas, volumes/corridors/LLTRs, EW AOPs, and J3.1/J3.5 message paths, while the main_flow only implements a J3.0 multisided-area definition path (descriptor value 3, continuation indicator, closing the area, Reference TN rule, and Surveillance Network PG transmission). The goal therefore conflates multiple distinct use cases or variants that the single main_flow cannot cover.

Alternative flow claim 3 (0-based index 2) says it diverges from a main-flow step in which the C2 JU reports a new J3.1 Emergency Point, but main_flow contains no J3.1 Emergency Point step. The main flow is entirely about reporting a multisided area using J3.0 messages, so this branch has no existing step to diverge from.

Alternative flow claim 4 (0-based index 3) says it diverges from a main-flow step in which the C2 JU prepares a J3.1 Emergency Point report, but main_flow has no J3.1 report-preparation step. The anchor for this branch does not exist in the supplied main flow.

Alternative flow claim 1 (0-based index 0) says it diverges from a main-flow step in which the C2 JU slaves a geometric area to a related TN, but no main_flow step contains a slaving operation. The main flow only assigns TNs, reports absolute geodetic positions, sets descriptor/continuation, closes the area, and establishes the Reference TN.

Alternative flow claim 5 (0-based index 4) says it diverges from a main-flow step in which the C2 JU modifies a reference point while retaining the same Reference TN, but main_flow has no modification step. It only defines a new multisided area and later uses the Reference TN as the identifier for that area.
